messages:
maria: quick question — after the TF change that consolidates per-model flags into a single ConfigMap, we're seeing occasional hot-reload collisions where pods briefly error on config apply. Any quick ideas on whether this is a controller debounce/ttl issue or TF doing multiple writes?
lee: can you paste the PR/link and one of the failing pod logs?
mar ia: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/243 — failure log from runtime controller below:
```
ERROR runtime-config-watcher: apply failed: Operation cannot be fulfilled on configmaps "model-flags": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again
```
maria: seems like a classic update conflict from simultaneous writes. but timing feels ~sub-second bursts so wondering if our hot-reload TTL (debounce) is too short.
sam: yup, this is likely two actors writing: (1) TF apply during deploy, (2) flag-sync daemon writing updates. If both do a Get->Modify->Update without retry-on-conflict you get that error.
tess: do we have retry-on-conflict in the controller? last i checked it was a simple Update.
sam: controller snippet we currently have uses client.CoreV1().ConfigMaps(ns).Update(ctx, cm, opts) after fetching — no retry loop. quick fix: wrap update in retry.RetryOnConflict(backoff.Default, func() error { ... }) or implement optimistic merge.
lee: +1. Another pragmatic pattern is to have the controller set an annotation checksum on the Deployment/DaemonSet so k8s handles pod restarts deterministically instead of live mutating ConfigMap that many pods watch. example annotation:
```
metadata:
  annotations:
    config.redwood.com/flags-checksum: "sha256:{{ checksum }}"
```
Then change the rolling logic by bumping checksum when config changes.
jonathan: fwiw, adding checksum to pod template will force restart (nice) but we still need to avoid transient double-writes from TF & controller.
maria: how bad are the errors? they're transient — pods retry and recover, but we had a brief 5% request error spike during the rollout. we want to avoid even that.
sam: three action options: (A) add RetryOnConflict in flag-sync/controller (low risk), (B) add short backoff + queueing to dedupe rapid writes (medium), (C) canonicalize source-of-truth so only TF writes and controller reads (larger infra change).
tess: i'd do A + B now. A is quick PR, B reduces likelihood of collisions under load.
lee: agree. also consider ordering for secret-sync: secret-sync writes secret then configmap; if those are in different controllers there's a race where configmap references secret that isn't ready yet. we saw that in one customer rollout. tighten ordering by wire a post-write hook in secret-sync to enqueue configmap update.
maria: noted. i'll open the PR for RetryOnConflict on controller. sam, can you add a small exponential backoff on the flag-sync side?
sam: yup, i'll open a PR tonight. will also add logs to count conflict retries so we can gauge how frequent they are.
lee: i'll prototype adding the checksum annotation to the deployment templates in a separate PR so we can canary it on a single model pool.
jonathan: we should also update our docs and runbook: what to do if a TF apply triggers many config writes. add a section: "if seeing \"object has been modified\" failures, check for concurrent controllers and enable retry/backoff".
infra-bot: deploy-check: infra/pr/243 build passed · integration tests green · canary=off
maria: thanks — next steps: 1) maria PR for RetryOnConflict (in review), 2) sam PR for backoff+metrics, 3) lee PR for checksum canary, 4) doc update (jonathan). I'll post links when available.
tess: small nit — consider increasing debounce TTL from 500ms to 2s for the watcher to collapse bursts. that plus RetryOnConflict should eliminate noise.
sam: +1. will include TTL change in my PR and add a config flag so we can tweak in prod without rebuild.
maria: sounds good. if anyone sees more errors after these changes ping me and tag @maria. thanks!
